title: I built a virtual civilization run entirely by autonomous AI agents with no pre-scripted behaviors (Demiurge)
author: United-Metal4470
selftext:
https://reddit.com/link/1tb2huw/video/al82lqyxpp0h1/player



Hi everyone!

For the past few months, I’ve been developing **'Demiurge'**, a virtual world populated by AI agents that reason, communicate, and maintain a society on their own. The core of this project is that **zero scripting** is involved for their high-level social behaviors.

**Here are the key highlights you can see in the demo:**

**1. Autonomous Supply Chain & Labor Division** The agents have no pre-defined paths. When the Food Department cultivates wheat, Cooks bake the bread, and Porters move it to the treasury. This entire supply chain is completed solely through real-time inter-agent communication. They act as "economic agents" rather than just simple NPCs.

**2. Emergent Collaborative Defense** Check out what happens in the middle of the video when I (the player) attack a worker. Instead of just fleeing individually, the 'War Director' perceives the threat and immediately shifts the collective into a 'Combat State.' The way the Strikers coordinate to flank and neutralize me demonstrates the strategic autonomy of this Multi-Agent System (MAS).

**3. Visualization of AI Reasoning (Left Log)** The logs on the left represent the agents' "brains." You can see their actual reasoning process in real-time—from personal needs like *"I'm hungry, seeking food"* to tactical commands like *"Intruder detected at (44, 56), converge now!"*

**4. Conflict Resolution & Routine Recovery** Once the threat is eliminated, the agents loot the intruder’s gear to recover resources and seamlessly return to their daily tasks (farming, crafting, etc.) as if nothing happened. My goal was to create a truly resilient and sustainable social simulation.

**I’m happy to dive deeper into the technical architecture or the logic behind this system. Please let me know if you have any questions or feedback—I'd love to hear your thoughts!**

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5mOdG0C6vrk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5mOdG0C6vrk)

comments.author: thirsty_pretzelzz
comments.body:
Very cool! 

So each characters every decision and action is a separate llm call? Does that get expensive even with a cheap model or is this all locally run?

replies.author: United-Metal4470
replies.body:
Thanks!

Not every action — that would be prohibitively expensive. The architecture has a tiered decision system:

\*\*LLM-driven\*\* (the interesting decisions):

\- Department-level orders (e.g., "Crafter1: craft 5 stone knives at CraftingTable\_51\_51")

\- Inter-agent communication and reporting

\- Strategic decisions (which task to take, when to flee, who to report to)

\- These happen at department-head and individual-agent levels, on irregular intervals based on context changes

\*\*Rule-based / state machine\*\* (the mechanical stuff):

\- Pathfinding, movement

\- Combat tick logic (damage calculation, hit detection)

\- Resource gathering animations

\- Inventory mechanics

\- Anything that has a clear deterministic answer

The split matters: LLMs decide \*what\* and \*why\*, the engine handles \*how\*. An agent doesn't need an LLM call to walk three tiles north — but does need one to decide where to walk and why.



\*\*On cost / hosting:\*\*

Currently using Gemini Flash Lite via API. With \~100 agents and the tiered architecture, it runs at a manageable cost, but API-based is not the production path.

Earlier iterations used fine-tuned Qwen-family models self-hosted on RunPod (custom training data generated from gameplay). That brought inference cost to roughly 1/10 of equivalent API usage, with comparable quality on the agent's actual task distribution. I'm currently re-applying that pipeline to the latest harness architecture — when stable, the system runs entirely on self-hosted GPUs.

The 4x playback speed in the demo is because of the current API-based inference latency. Native real-time comes with the self-hosted fine-tuned setup.

replies.body: maybe you can keep a few agents running on the major llm apis. See if they perform better or get outcast.

replies.author: United-Metal4470
replies.body:
That is a fascinating experiment idea! Testing a mixed-intelligence society where some agents run on top-tier APIs (like GPT-5.5 or Opus 4.7) while others use smaller local models would be a great way to observe social stratification.



I'm curious to see if the high-reasoning agents naturally emerge as leaders or planners, and whether the less capable ones get outcast or simply fill more routine, manual labor roles. It could essentially become a simulation of how different cognitive abilities shape social hierarchies and economic structures.



Definitely adding this to my research roadmap. Thanks for the inspiration!

replies.author: Melodic-Upstairs7584
replies.body: Self hosted models on a local system aren’t sufficient for this?

replies.author: United-Metal4470
replies.body: Thanks for your interest! While I'm moving toward a self-hosted setup, my current local machine isn't fully optimized for high-throughput LLM inference. Handling dozens of concurrent agent streams with low latency requires specialized hardware performance that my current setup can't yet provide. Since the fluidity of the social simulation depends on near-instant responses, I'm focusing on building an environment that can sustain those high inference speeds.

replies.author: United-Metal4470
replies.body:
Great question! To put it simply: **Traditional games are scripted "movies," but Demiurge aims to be a living, emergent "ecosystem."**

Think of a game like **GTA 5**. If you commit a crime, the police "spawn" from thin air because a script told them to. In our world, there is no such script. Instead, a witness agent reports the crime, a bureaucratic agent processes it, and an officer agent is dispatched from a physical location.

**Our Vision: A Civilization Built from the Bottom Up**

We are building toward a future where every pillar of society is constructed by AI agents, not pre-authored by developers:

* **Autonomous Economy:** Prices and supply chains aren't fixed. They emerge from agents deciding what to produce, trade, and consume based on their individual needs and departmental goals.
* **Internal Social Dynamics:** Within a single city, agents form their own laws, cultural norms, and hierarchical organizations (like the bureaucratic systems and labor unions) through inter-agent communication.
* **International Diplomacy:** Relations between different nations—be it trade treaties or declarations of war—aren't triggered by quest flags. They are the result of collective reasoning and strategic decisions made by agent-led governments.

**Current Status & The Road Ahead**

To be clear, we are currently in the **prototype stage**. We have successfully implemented core labor division and collective defense logic, but we haven't reached the scale of full nations or complex macro-economies yet.

However, as **LLM inference costs continue to plummet**, we believe the technical bottleneck for massive, agent-run civilizations will soon disappear. We are building the foundational architecture now so that we can support thousands of agents simulating entire, unscripted histories in real-time.

Soon, the value of a virtual world won't be measured by its graphical fidelity, but by the **depth and complexity of the autonomous history** its agents have written.
